current.title: Corpus spongiosum · bulb/shaft source · CT: urethral contrast is not the erectile-tissue boundary · draft
current.body: The corpus spongiosum is tissue around the spongy urethra, not the urethral passage itself. Dedicated CT retrograde urethrography introduces contrast into that passage; its opacified route must not be mistaken for the complete outline of the surrounding corpus spongiosum.
bullets: An original prospective CT-urethrography study included 22 men with urethral abnormalities. Its selected clinical cohort is not evidence that routine CT consistently resolves normal spongiosal boundaries.

The investigators did not measure surrounding spongiofibrosis thickness on CT, explaining that similar attenuation of scar and adjacent erectile tissue limited that assessment. This is a study-specific limitation, not a normal measurement or a treatment recommendation.

This source-labelled bulb/shaft surface supplies no glans, tunical layers or validated urethral lumen. It is not a CT segmentation; neither a smooth surface nor the separate urethral model establishes tissue integrity, patency or a measured fibrosis boundary.

Source limit: Original source-labelled bulb/shaft representation. The separately supplied glans and corporal surfaces are not added; this is not the complete corpus spongiosum or penis. The existing urethra is context, not a validated enclosed lumen. Original coordinates and faces retained; clinical review pending.

Reference: Berna-Mestre and colleagues (2021), prospective CT retrograde urethrography study, especially its stated tissue-assessment limits; NCI SEER, Penis. No acquisition, contrast-dose, instrumentation or treatment instructions supplied.
current.note: Educational draft for revision-bound radiologist review, not a diagnostic test or procedure plan. No patient registration, scan or clinical approval is supplied. Atlas, imaging-case and paid-lecture access remain independent.
